title: TrustLeak Finding
description: A single trust-relationship finding produced by TrustLeak, correlating an active application with a subdomain flagged by ShadowSaaS. This is the contract consumed by the (future) Graph Analyzer / TrustPath — any tool emitting or reading this shape should validate against schema_version before trusting the rest of the document.

schema_version.description: Pinned to the exact version this document's shape was written against. A consumer must reject (not best-effort-parse) any value it doesn't explicitly handle.

finding_id.description: Stable identifier for this finding, e.g. 'TL-0001'. Used for dedup and for referencing a finding from the graph.

hostname.description: The active application that was found referencing the target.

type.description: Reserved for future source kinds (e.g. 'mobile_app', 'config_file'); only 'active_application' exists in v1.

hostname.description: The subdomain flagged by ShadowSaaS that 'source' references.

asset_status.description: Carried over from ShadowSaaS's own takeover_possible/confidence — TrustLeak does not re-derive this, it just quotes it.

shadowsaas_confidence.description: ShadowSaaS's confidence field for this target, copied verbatim. Optional only because a target might reach TrustLeak via a non-ShadowSaaS source in the future (see from_url/external ingestion note in the source-of-truth doc).

type.description: What kind of trust relationship connects source to target. New types must be added here explicitly — no free-text types, so the Graph Analyzer never has to handle an edge type it's never seen.

status.description: 'observed' = reference exists in the evidence, effect not tested. 'potential_risk' = reference plus a corroborating signal (e.g. CSP reference to a ShadowSaaS high-confidence target). 'validated' = actively tested and the trust relationship was confirmed to have effect (e.g. CORS origin reflection confirmed against a controlled Origin header). Never use 'confirmed' here — that word is reserved for a human-reviewed finding in the pentest report, not an automated correlation.

source_url.description: The exact URL the evidence was observed on.

header.description: The HTTP header the evidence came from, if applicable (e.g. 'Content-Security-Policy').

directive.description: For CSP: the directive matched (e.g. 'img-src'). Omitted for non-CSP relationship types.

matched_value.description: The literal value that matched the target hostname.

collected_via.description: Provenance: 'shadowsaas_probe' means this header was already captured by ShadowSaaS's own http_probe() and TrustLeak only read it — no extra request was made. 'trustleak_active_request' means TrustLeak made its own request (e.g. to test CORS origin reflection, which requires sending a controlled Origin header ShadowSaaS never sends). This distinction matters for anyone auditing what traffic actually left the scanner during an engagement.

confidence.description: TrustLeak's own confidence in this specific finding — distinct from target.shadowsaas_confidence, which is ShadowSaaS's confidence in the takeover itself. The two can disagree: a low-confidence ShadowSaaS target referenced via a high-confidence CSP match still yields a finding worth a human's attention, just not an automatic escalation.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this finding was produced, not when the evidence was collected (see evidence.source_url for that context).
